title: introduce-microtrace-rollups-and-reservoir-histograms-to-reduce-span-cardinality
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Long-lived and high-cardinality traces (very long token sequences, rare model paths, expensive fallbacks) are a dominant storage and query cost in our span store and make tail-latency debugging noisy. This PR implements a two-stage observability strategy: (1) microtrace rollups - compress long contiguous sequences of low-variance spans into a summarized microtrace that preserves aggregate timing, error counts, and representative exemplar spans; (2) reservoir histogram sampling for span durations and token-cost buckets so we keep high-fidelity distribution summaries without storing every sample.

Design summary: We add a rollup stage in the agent pipeline that identifies contiguous spans matching a heuristic (same route/model-instance, no error flags, contiguous token generation spans) and replaces them with a single summarized span that includes: count, total_duration_ms, p95_estimate_ms, exemplar_span_id, and a compact histogram key. For global metrics we emit reservoir-based histograms (bounded memory, sliding-window TTL) keyed by route/model/tenant that feed dashboards and alerts. The histogram implementation uses a fixed-size reservoir + decay window to ensure fresh tail visibility.

Compatibility and data model: Rollups are an additive transformation before storage and tag a span with label rollup.v=1. Existing consumers will see summarized spans alongside regular spans - we also keep one exemplar for each rollup so trace replays can expand the representative path for debugging. The new histogram keys are exported to the metrics pipeline under metrics.obs.rollup_hist.<aggregation> to avoid colliding with current metric names.

Operational plan: Default rollout to hosted and staging private deployments with config toggle redwood.obs.rollups.enabled=false. We will enable in small canaries for 48 hours and monitor: storage ingested size, query latencies for trace search, number of trace matches that include rollup spans, and user-facing debugging coverage (tracked via Linear ENG-2743).

Dashboards and alerts: New dashboards added: "Microtrace Rollup Overview" (storage delta, rollup ratio by route/model, exemplar coverage), "Reservoir Histogram Explorer" (approx distributions and tail percentiles), and a trace-search toggle to filter rollup vs full traces. Alerts adjusted: lowered noise on trace-store-queue-depth by 10% during rollout and added an alert when exemplar coverage < 99% for any high-SLA tenant.

Testing & validation: Unit tests for rollup heuristics and exemplar selection, load tests simulating 10k QPS long-sequence generation to validate memory bounds, and end-to-end test against local metrics pipeline. Manual verifications included sampling expanded exemplar traces and comparing end-to-end token-cost aggregates to ensure rollups do not alter billing math.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement rollup algorithm and exemplar retention
- [x] Add reservoir histogram implementation and exporter
- [x] Update dashboards and alert rules (Grafana + PagerDuty runbook draft)
- [x] Feature flag + canary rollout plan
- [x] Unit and integration tests

Related: touches on work in ENG-2817 (trace-query optimizations) and SUP-912 (support incident that exposed high-card span storms).
